scope_note: Per user decision Q-1, only commit 140f27e is reviewed: tests/ci/retry.sudo.test.ts and the EPERM-tolerant killGroup in tools/ci/retry.js. Round 1 had no BLOCKER/MAJOR findings. Round-1 MINOR tools/ci/retry.js:sudo-use-pty-escapes-group-kill is now covered by a real-environment test.

rubric.item: Q-1.1 Linux-CI sudo hang test: correctness (2 s timeout, 2 attempts, 0 s delay, sudo -n hanging sleep, two timeout warnings, exit 1 + ::error:: line, < 20 s, no marker process left)
Q-1.1 test strength (fails if sudo-run processes survive or the helper crashes)
Q-1.1 skip condition (linux && CI === 'true'; ci.yml runs npm test on ubuntu-24.04, where GitHub sets CI=true and sudo is passwordless)
Q-1.1 cannot leave a hanging sleep on the runner

findings.issue: The happy path leaves nothing behind. If the test fails, though, it does no cleanup. (a) If the sudo'd sleep survives, it is root-owned and runs for about 1000 s (the marker is the sleep duration, which is much longer than the 120 s the Q-1 note suggested). (b) If the helper itself hangs, for example after an EPERM on every signal, the 30 s Vitest timeout abandons the test but does not kill the helper or its sudo/sleep. Also, if a surviving process inherited the helper's stdout pipe, waiting on 'close' never resolves. The test then fails as an opaque 30 s timeout instead of on the pgrep assertion. In every case the test still fails, so this is not a false pass. The GitHub runner's end-of-job orphan-process cleanup also kills the leftovers, so the job will not hang. But the user explicitly asked that the test cannot leave a hanging sleep, and on these failure paths it can until the job ends.
findings.evidence: Line 66 resolves on child 'close'. There is no try/finally, no child.kill, and no privileged pkill. The marker `1000.<9 digits>` is passed as sleep's duration (lines 44, 62).
findings.fix: Wrap the body in try/finally. In finally, call child.kill('SIGKILL') if it is still running and `spawnSync('sudo', ['-n', 'pkill', '-KILL', '-f', marker])`, so the assertions still run first. Resolve on 'exit' rather than 'close', so a leaked pipe holder shows up as the pgrep failure. Optionally lower the sleep to about 120 s, for example `120.<digits>`.

summary: killGroup now logs and swallows EPERM, swallows ESRCH, and rethrows anything else. The exported killGroup is exercised by three mocked-process.kill unit tests that run on every platform. Those tests would fail if EPERM or ESRCH were rethrown or if other errors were swallowed, and they pass locally (3 passed, 1 skipped on macOS). The Linux-CI test matches Q-1. It wraps `sudo -n sh -c 'exec sleep "$1"' sh <marker>`, so sudo, sh and sleep all carry the marker in argv, and pgrep -f covers all three; pgrep excludes itself, and spawnSync runs it without a shell. It also asserts exactly two `timed out after 2 s` warnings, exit 1, the ::error:: last line, and < 20 s. A helper crash, which is an uncaught throw in the timer or finish path, happens before any timeout warning is logged, so the match is null and the test fails. Surviving sudo children fail either the pgrep check or the 30 s timeout. A SIGTERM that sudo does not relay pushes the run to about 24 s because of the 10 s SIGKILL grace period, and that fails the < 20 s check. If `sudo -n` is refused, the attempts fail fast with an exit code instead of timing out, so the test fails rather than passing falsely. The skip condition is right for ubuntu-24.04 GitHub-hosted runners. The test was not executed here because it is skipped on macOS, so its real behaviour is proven only by the first CI run. There are no BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. One MINOR finding: there is no cleanup on the failure path, so a root-owned sleep of about 1000 s can outlive a failing test until the runner's end-of-job orphan cleanup kills it.
